process_area.title: Equipment Maintenance, Safety, Compliance & Fleet Utilization Analytics

value_stream.name: Compact & Heavy Construction Equipment Rental Fleet Operations

fields.Frequency: ~1 PM per unit per ~250 operating hours; ~1,500–2,500 PM events/yr
fields.Participants: Mechanics, Parts Clerk, OEM Service Partner
fields.Trigger: Telematics hour-meter threshold (W5324); calendar PM; return inspection flagged (W5334)

workflows.name: Heavy Equipment Preventive Maintenance Schedule, Service Bay & Mechanic Operations

Automation Opportunity: - PM auto-scheduled from telematics; parts min-max auto-reorder; availability auto-restored on PM close.
Controls: - CTL-104: rental-fleet PM & availability integrity; operational: no-unit-to-Available-without-PM-close.
Cross-references: - links to VS-12.2 (W1554 power-tool PM, W1172 fleet lifecycle), VS-20.3 (facility/bay), VS-05 (parts inventory)
Pain Points / Risks: - **In-field-breakdown risk**: PM deferred past the threshold causes a failure on a customer's jobsite (lost rental day + recovery cost + reputational hit); mitigated by auto-generated PM work-orders and a hard availability-hold until PM closes.
- **Parts-stockout risk**: a unit grounded for weeks waiting for a hydraulic seal not in the kit; mitigated by the W5322 minimum spares kit and min-max parts replenishment.
System Touchpoints: - CMMS / maintenance work-order module (per-asset); parts inventory (VS-05); rental availability status; telematics hour-meter trigger.

steps.activity: Auto-generate PM work-order from the hour-meter threshold; pull the unit from availability.
Execute class-specific PM (engine oil, hydraulics, filters, tracks/tires, safety devices, electrics) in the service bay.
Replace wear parts from the on-hand kit (W5322); raise parts-replenishment if below min.
Record PM completion, hour-meter-in, parts used, and mechanic hours in the asset history.
Return unit to Available; notify any waitlist (VS-12.2 W1318).

fields.Participants: Field Service Tech/OEM, Logistics Dispatcher, Customer, Credit/Billing
fields.Trigger: In-rental breakdown reported by customer or telematics fault code

workflows.name: Equipment Breakdown, Field Service Dispatch & Substitute Unit Provisioning

Automation Opportunity: - Telematics fault code auto-opens a case and suggests field-repair vs. swap-out; auto-source nearest substitute unit.
Controls: - CTL-104: breakdown-repair accountability & substitute-unit recovery; operational: downtime no-charge rule for non-customer-caused failures.
Cross-references: - links to VS-12 (installation/service dispatch), VS-06 (logistics), VS-31 (quality/root-cause)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Customer-loss risk**: a breakdown without a substitute unit loses the rental and the customer to a competitor; mitigated by a documented substitute-unit SLA and a small float reserve at each hub.
- **Mis-charging risk**: charging the customer for BuildRight's equipment failure erodes trust; mitigated by a downtime no-charge rule for non-customer-caused failures.
System Touchpoints: - Field-service/dispatch (VS-06/VS-12); substitute-unit availability; rental billing adjustment; asset repair history.

steps.activity: Triage the reported fault (telematics code + customer description); decide field-repair vs. swap-out.
Dispatch a field service tech or OEM partner to the jobsite (links VS-12/VS-06 dispatch).
If swap-out: source a substitute unit, deliver (W5331), and hand over (W5330) to keep the customer's job running (VS-12.2 W1374 pattern).
Recover the broken unit to the bay; diagnose, repair, and route to PM (W5337).
Adjust billing (no-charge for downtime), and capture root-cause for fleet-quality feedback to procurement (W5322).

fields.Frequency: Annual per registered unit; ad-hoc for crane/rigging permits
fields.Participants: LTO/LTFRB liaison, Rental Fleet Manager, Permit Portfolio (VS-166)
fields.Trigger: Unit intake (registered/titled equipment); annual registration renewal; permit expiry

workflows.name: Equipment LTO/LTFRB Registration, Crane/Rigging Permit & Roadworthiness Compliance

Automation Opportunity: - Permit-expiry alerts auto-gate availability; renewal applications pre-filled from the asset register.
Controls: - CTL-41: LGU/agency regulatory compliance; CTL-26 (permit-validity availability gate).
Cross-references: - links to VS-166 (permit portfolio), VS-165 (PCAB contractor licensing), VS-76 (LGU compliance), VS-06 (fleet registration)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Operating-illegal risk**: renting out an unregistered or expired-permit unit (e.g. an overdue crane permit) exposes BuildRight to LTFRB/LGU fines, impound, and operator personal liability; mitigated by an availability gate that blocks rental of expired units.
- **Lapse risk**: a permit that lapses unnoticed takes a unit (and its revenue) out of availability; mitigated by 60-day expiry alerts in the permit portfolio.
System Touchpoints: - Permit/portfolio register (VS-166) with expiry alerts; rental availability gate on permit validity.

steps.activity: Identify which units require LTO/LTFRB registration (self-propelled/road-going) vs. plant-only equipment.
File/renew registration, emission, and roadworthiness (annual); obtain plates/decals.
For crane/aerial/rigging classes, secure and renew the specific operating permits (links VS-165 PCAB/contractor).
Record permits in the license/permit portfolio with expiry alerts (VS-166).
Gate rental availability on valid registration/permit; block rental of expired units.

fields.Frequency: Annual certification per certified unit; per-shift logbook
fields.Participants: DOLE-accredited inspector, Mechanics, Rental Yard Lead
fields.Trigger: Annual DOLE equipment certification; per-use logbook; regulatory inspection

workflows.name: Operator Safety Compliance, DOLE-OSH Equipment Certification & Plant-Equipment Logbook

Automation Opportunity: - Digital pre-use check app feeding the logbook; certification-expiry alerts auto-gate availability.
Controls: - CTL-790 (ensure controlled execution — Equipment Maintenance, Safety, Compliance & Fleet Utilization Analytics (PA-186.3).)
Cross-references: - links to VS-24 (HSE), VS-166 (permits), VS-22 (compliance), VS-115 (calibration of safety devices)
Pain Points / Risks: - **DOLE-finding risk**: an uncertified or expired piece of lifting/pressure equipment operated at a customer site triggers a DOLE OSH finding and officer personal liability (RA 11058); mitigated by the availability gate and annual certification scheduling.
- **Logbook-gap risk**: a missing pre-use logbook entry undermines incident defense (W5341); mitigated by a digital logbook with a mandatory pre-use check before handover.
System Touchpoints: - Asset certification register (VS-166); digital logbook capturing pre-use checks; availability gate on certification validity.
Time Estimate: - ~1–2 weeks elapsed per annual certification cycle fleet-wide; logbook entries ~5 min each.

steps.activity: Schedule DOLE-accredited third-party certification for pressure/lift/earthmoving equipment (per DOLE OSH standards).
Maintain the per-unit plant-equipment logbook: pre-use checks, faults, and rectifications (DOLE requirement).
Verify safety devices (emergency stop, overload alarm, fall protection anchors) at each PM (W5337) and handover (W5330).
Record certifications in the asset history and permit portfolio (VS-166); gate availability on valid certification.
Respond to DOLE inspection findings and document corrective action (links VS-24/VS-22).

fields.Participants: Rental Fleet Manager, Legal (VS-100), Insurance (VS-26), Corporate Security (VS-159), Customer, Police
fields.Trigger: Accident/injury/third-party damage involving rented equipment (at jobsite or in transit)

workflows.name: Equipment Rental Accident, Injury & Third-Party Damage Incident Management

Automation Opportunity: - Incident-report app that auto-pulls telematics/logbook/competency evidence and starts the insurance/DOLE notice clock.
Controls: - CTL-104: rental-incident recovery — fraud detection in claims; CTL-219 (asset-register evidence); operational: 48h insurance/DOLE notice SLA.
Cross-references: - links to VS-24 (HSE), VS-26 (insurance), VS-100 (legal), VS-159 (security), VS-147 (customer/premises safety), VS-133 (lessons-learned)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Liability-exposure risk**: a serious injury (e.g. aerial-lift fall) without documented competency/safety-briefing evidence exposes BuildRight to large damages; mitigated by the W5326/W5330 documentation chain.
- **Notice-window risk**: late insurance/DOLE notification forfeits coverage or compounds the regulatory finding; mitigated by a 24–48h notice SLA embedded in incident response.
System Touchpoints: - Incident/case module (VS-24/VS-23); telematics replay; insurance claim register (VS-26); DOLE-reportable filing.

steps.activity: Secure the scene and ensure medical aid; preserve the unit and evidence (DOLE reportable threshold).
Capture incident facts: telematics (W5332), logbook (W5340), operator competency record (W5326), and witness statements.
Notify insurance/captive within the policy notice window (W5327/VS-26); file DOLE reportable if applicable (VS-24).
Coordinate legal defense and third-party claim handling (VS-100/VS-26); engage Corporate Security for fraud/foul-play (VS-159).
Root-cause analysis; corrective action to fleet/PM/training (W5337/W5326); capture lessons-learned (VS-133).

fields.Volume: 1 review per hub weekly; 1 group review monthly

workflows.name: Fleet Utilization, Idle-Time, Rate-Realization & Yield Analytics

Automation Opportunity: - Auto-refreshing utilization/yield dashboard from telematics + billing; auto-flag classes below the utilization hurdle.
Controls: - CTL-790 (ensure controlled execution — Equipment Maintenance, Safety, Compliance & Fleet Utilization Analytics (PA-186.3).)
- operational: performance vs. business-case hurdle; utilization-data accuracy; .
Cross-references: - links to VS-28 (BI/analytics), VS-118 (revenue assurance), VS-12.2 (W1376 rental analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stranded-asset risk**: a class sitting at 30% utilization erodes the capex hurdle silently; mitigated by weekly utilization review with explicit rebalance/reprice/disposition decisions.
- **Attach-blindness risk**: renting equipment that doesn't lift material sales under-cuts the business case (W5321); mitigated by attach-lift measurement in the dashboard.
System Touchpoints: - BI/analytics on the telematics + billing + rental-lifecycle data (VS-28); fleet-performance dashboard.

steps.activity: Compute utilization (rented-hours ÷ available-hours) and idle-time by class, hub, and region from telematics.
Compute realized rate vs. rate card (W5325) and yield (revenue ÷ capex) per class.
Identify under-utilized classes/hubs → rebalancing (W5344), repricing (W5325), or disposition (W5343).
Benchmark attach-to-material-sales lift (does renting a mixer lift a cement/aggregate basket?).
Publish the fleet-performance dashboard to the Services leadership.

fields.Participants: Finance (Asset Accountant), Procurement (W5322), VS-35, Used-equipment buyer
fields.Trigger: Unit hits lifecycle age/hours; chronic high-repair-cost flag; or category exit

workflows.name: Fleet Age, Lifecycle Replacement, Disposition & Trade-In Management

Automation Opportunity: - Lifecycle-candidate auto-flag from age/hours/repair-cost; disposal valuation from used-equipment-market data.
Controls: - CTL-26: fixed asset disposal; CTL-27 (telematics/customer-data wipe before disposal).
Cross-references: - links to VS-35 (fixed assets), VS-40 (replacement capex), VS-155 (trade-in), VS-12.2 (W1172 fleet lifecycle), VS-99 (IT/asset disposal)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Run-to-failure risk**: keeping units past economic life inflates repair cost and breakdown frequency (W5338); mitigated by lifecycle-decision triggers on age/hours/repair-cost.
- **Disposal-leakage risk**: disposing of a PHP 3M unit below market or without telematics wipe; mitigated by a disposal valuation and mandatory device-data wipe (links VS-99/VS-91).
System Touchpoints: - Fixed Asset retirement/disposal (VS-35/CTL-26); replacement capex (VS-40); trade-in/B2B sale order (VS-11/VS-155).
Time Estimate: - ~2–4 weeks elapsed per disposition batch; ~80/yr → ~600 person-hours/yr.

steps.activity: Identify lifecycle candidates from age, operating hours, and repair-cost-trend (W5337).
Decide refurbish vs. replace vs. dispose based on remaining economic life and the replacement capex (W5321/VS-40).
For replacement: order the successor unit (W5322) and plan the swap to minimize availability gap.
Dispose via trade-in to OEM, sale to used-equipment buyer, or VS-155 trade-in/B2B sale; ensure data/device wipe on telematics.
Retire the asset from the register, recognize gain/loss, and update the fleet plan (VS-35).

fields.Participants: Supply Planning (VS-02/VS-127), Logistics Dispatcher, Store Managers
fields.Trigger: Utilization imbalance (W5342); seasonal demand shift; new hub ramp

workflows.name: Cross-Store Equipment Rebalancing, Inter-DC Transport & Demand Seasonality Planning

Automation Opportunity: - Utilization-imbalance auto-suggests rebalancing moves; transfer order auto-created and telematics re-homes on arrival.
Cross-references: - links to VS-06 (logistics/transfers), VS-02/VS-127 (planning/forecast), VS-12.2 (W1553 cross-store rebalancing)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mis-positioning risk**: a high-demand unit stuck at a low-demand hub while another hub stock-outs loses the rental and ships a substitute long-distance; mitigated by monthly utilization-driven rebalancing.
- **In-transit risk**: a PHP 5M unit damaged/lost in an inter-hub transfer; mitigated by in-transit insurance and telematics tracking (links VS-25/CTL-25).
System Touchpoints: - Rental-asset home-location + transfer orders (VS-05/VS-06); demand forecast (VS-02/VS-127); telematics re-home confirmation.
Time Estimate: - ~2 person-hours per transfer + dispatcher effort; ~300/yr → ~1,000 person-hours/yr.

steps.activity: Map demand vs. fleet by hub/region and season (rainy-season dewatering pumps, summer concrete equipment, etc.).
Identify rebalancing moves from low- to high-demand hubs using utilization (W5342) and forecast (VS-127).
Execute inter-DC/store transfers via logistics (W5331/VS-06) with in-transit insurance (VS-25/VS-26).
Update the rental-asset home-location and availability ledger; confirm telematics re-home.
Review post-season rebalancing effectiveness and feed the next season's fleet plan (W5321).
